question.text: Within bonds, treasury bonds, corporate bonds and junk bonds are examples of:

answer.text: Sub-asset classes within the bond asset class

explanation.text: The Logic: The broad 'bonds' asset class can be split into sub-asset classes by issuer/credit. The Trap: They all share the bond asset class — the distinction is credit/issuer, not class. Cross-Exam Context: NISM IV (IRD) and X-A make the same split. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Use sub-asset-class diversification for more granular risk control in PMS portfolios.
